tier_reason: The README's speed-up over RBush is qualitative ('Faster indexing and search'); its benchmark table and bench.js measure Flatbush alone, so there are no baseline numbers and the comparison is D.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README says Flatbush is similar to RBush with 'Faster indexing and search, with much lower memory footprint'; no RBush timings or ratio appear on the page. Flatbush-only numbers ('node bench.js' on a MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Node v24): index 1,000,000 rectangles 109ms; 100 searches 10% area 64ms; 1000 searches 1% area 66ms; 10000 searches 0.1% area 150ms; 10000 searches 0.01% area 51ms; 10000 searches 0.001% area 31ms; 10000 searches of 1 neighbor 30ms; 10000 searches of 100 neighbors 127ms; 1 search of 1,000,000 neighbors 84ms.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Node v24 (README); no other settings stated
corrections.caveats: The speed-up over RBush is a qualitative README claim: the benchmark table has only a flatbush column and bench.js imports only ./index.js (seeded mulberry32 data, nodeSize 16, 10 repetitions), never RBush. RBush's own README performance table dates from Node 6.2.2 on a mid-2012 MacBook Pro and compares RBush with an older RTree, so no fair Flatbush/RBush ratio can be derived from the two pages. Not C++ and not compared with Boost.Geometry or CGAL. The README lists C++ ports (chusitoo/flatbush; IMQS/flatbush, no longer maintained) and Rust/C#/Python/Dart ports. Kept as a tier D entry because of notability (1.6k stars).

notes: Numbers on the page match the record but are Flatbush-only; tier D for the RBush claim confirmed. Metadata checked: ISC, 1.6k stars, last commit 2026-07-08, not a fork. JavaScript; its C++ port chusitoo/flatbush is a possible seed lead.
